stemMd: A sphere is viewed orthographically from above, from the front and from the side. What is true of its three external silhouettes?

options.label: A
options.textMd: They become smaller in the more distant view

options.label: D
options.textMd: One is an ellipse and two are circles

options.label: E
options.textMd: They are circles with different diameters

explanationMd: A sphere is rotationally symmetric about every axis through its centre. Its orthographic silhouette is a circle with the sphere’s radius in every viewing direction. Thus all three silhouettes are congruent.

distractorRationale.d: A sphere has the same radius in every direction.
distractorRationale.e: Orthographic view direction does not change the sphere’s radius.
distractorRationale.c: A sphere has no straight external edges.
distractorRationale.a: Orthographic projection has no distance-dependent scale.
